findings.GL2: Removed optional persisting-cache requests program residency; release or zero-size requests write a flush register without polling. No retained evidence establishes invocation during the stall. Initialization instrumentation only reads these registers; threshold setting is a software shadow. Saved activation reads show zero residency.
findings.GL2_address: The old flush-register source comment expects 0x18314, while the saved AID0 SOC15 address is 0x10194; BASE_IDX was marked a placeholder. This discrepancy is conditional on the unproved optional write path executing.
findings.PM4: The retained ROCr ACQUIRE_MEM requests GL2_INV with GL2_WB unset. It identifies the requested operation, not a hardware execution PC or the cause of nonprogress.
findings.retry: Old initialization readbacks differ only at VMID0. Subsequent KFD retry branches/masks and full sh_mem_config delivery to MES are preserved; selected compiled differences are device-structure displacement changes, and MES add-queue function bytes match. No user-queue retry-policy change or final live state is demonstrated.
findings.next_discriminators: After completed current validation and storage admission, screen a fresh process with only full FBGEMM prewarm removed. Prior prewarm on the same boot limits a pass. A fresh-boot matched current-source baseline/corrected controlled trap test can isolate CWSR from the reinstall changes.

limits: No firmware image was acquired or changed, and no GPU/register operation was performed for this analysis.
The user-reported 0x17d remove_queue defect does not prove a defect in actual 0x7b or identify prior per-run MES versions.
Source plausibility does not attribute the historical loader wait or weaken the deterministic CWSR corruption proof.
